title: Even-intersecting families of lattice paths and the Catalan numbers

creators.name: Bhattacharjee, Deep
creators.affiliation: Formerly, Electro-Gravitational Space Propulsion Laboratory (EGSPL), Bhubaneswar, Odisha 751030, India

description:
Shankar proved that a family of North–East lattice paths from (0,0) to (n,n) in which any two paths share an even number of edges has at most 2n members, and conjectured that exactly Cn families attain this bound, where Cn is the nth Catalan number (arXiv:2607.23117, Conjecture 4.1). We prove the conjecture: every extremal family is FM for a noncrossing perfect matching M. The proof determines all equality cases of the inequality behind Shankar's bound: they correspond to noncrossing partial matchings of {1,…,m} whose unmatched points lie under no arc, and there are C(m,⌊m/2⌋) of them.

The archive contains the paper (PDF, LaTeX source with the figures as PNG, arXiv tarball) and independent checks in C, C++, Bash, Python, Julia and Lean 4: the rigidity lemma of Section 4 for words of length up to 13, an exhaustive search and a SAT enumeration of all extremal systems for word lengths up to 5 and 6, Shankar's conjecture for n ≤ 5 by SAT, and Lean kernel checks of the key lemmas and of the conjecture for n ≤ 3.
